wu: Warm-up: Halloween Count Circle. Children stand in a circle, pass a plastic pumpkin, and count 1-10 forwards. Teacher says 'One', child passes to next and says 'Two', etc. If a child hesitates, they do a spooky action like 'Boo!'
wuAlt: Alternative 1: Number Flashcard Jump. Teacher shows number flashcards 1-10, children jump the number of times shown.
Alternative 2: Spooky Whisper. Children whisper 'One ghost, two cats...' while passing a toy around the circle.
pres: Presentation: Big Halloween Poster. Teacher shows a large poster with 10 Halloween items (bats, pumpkins, ghosts). Models 'How many pumpkins? One, two, three.' Children repeat. Teacher points and asks 'How many bats?' Children respond with numbers. Checks with thumbs up/down.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Mystery Bag. Teacher puts 10 plastic spiders in a bag, children guess 'How many?' before counting.
Alternative 2: Halloween Storybook. Read 'Ten Spooky Spiders', counting each page aloud.
prac: Guided Practice: Cut-and-Stick Poster. Children receive a poster with 10 unlabelled Halloween items and number stickers 1-10. They work in pairs to match numbers to items, saying 'One pumpkin, two bats...' as they stick. Teacher circulates to help.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: Number Bingo. Teacher calls numbers 1-10, children cover the corresponding pictures on their bingo cards.
Alternative 2: Halloween Memory Game. Children turn over number cards and Halloween picture cards, saying 'Two ghosts' when they match.
ls: Listening Slot: How Many? Game. Teacher plays a recording of spooky sounds (e.g., one howl, two bangs). Children hold up the correct number of fingers. Teacher asks 'How many sounds?' Children say the number. Checks with number flashcards.
re: Reactivation Game: Monster Count Freeze. Children dance to Halloween music. When music stops, teacher shouts a number (e.g., 'Four!'), children freeze in groups of four and say 'Four monsters!'
prod: Production Task: My Pumpkin Craft. Children draw and decorate a paper pumpkin. They present it to the class saying 'This is my pumpkin. It is big/scary!' Classmates ask 'How many eyes?' and the child answers.
rw: Reading/Writing Slot: Number Mini-Book. Children trace and copy number words 1-10 in a mini-book with Halloween pictures (e.g., 'One bat'). They read the book to a partner, pointing to each word.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Sing 'Five Little Pumpkins' song with actions. Read a short Halloween story about counting. Goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Children cover pictures on their bingo cards as teacher calls numbers 1-10.
Children roll a die, say the number, and draw that many pumpkin seeds on their paper.
Teacher says a costume word (e.g., 'witch'), children jump the number of letters.
Children count 1-10 while tossing a soft pumpkin.
Children hide paper ghosts around the room, then ask 'How many?' and count them.
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a spooky scene with 10 items, label them in English.
Support: Use number lines or trace dotted numbers for the craft.
hw: Homework 1: Read your numbers 1-10 mini-book to someone at home.
Homework 2: Draw your costume and label it in English (e.g., 'My mask is red').
Homework 3: Count 10 things in your house and tell your family in English.
tip: Use local Halloween-like traditions (like 'Aicha's wedding' sweets) to make the theme relatable. Pair strong and weak learners during craft activities to encourage peer support.
